cases.what: a peer with no host and no network is refused when the program is compiled

refuses: the court of doors refuses this literal -- PEER_NOWHERE: PEER a names no host: give it HOST, or NET for a network by its prefix; written

judged: PEER a names no host: give it HOST, or NET for a network by its prefix
DEFINE PEER b AS (HOST "x.org", NET "10.0.0.0/8") RATIONALE "x"
PEER b says HOST and NET: it is one or the other
DEFINE PEER c AS (HOST "Bad_Host!", SCHEMES [https]) RATIONALE "x"
'Bad_Host!' cannot be a host: a name on the wire is lowercase letters, digits and the hyphen, in labels separated by dots
DEFINE PEER d AS (HOST "x.org", SCHEMES [gopher]) RATIONALE "x"
A peer is reached by https, http, wss, ws or tcp, not 'gopher'
DEFINE PEER e AS (NET "10.0.0.0", SCHEMES [http]) RATIONALE "x"
